title: A CI job may only read inputs that a fresh checkout has
rule: When a workflow step reads a folder or file from the repository (a fuzz corpus, fixtures, a baseline, generated data), check that the path is tracked: `git ls-files <path>` is not empty and `git check-ignore <path>` finds no rule. Data that lives only in a developer's working tree (a gitignored corpus, a local cache) is absent on the runner, so the step fails before it does anything. Commit a (minimized) copy under an un-ignored path, or create or fetch it in the job, and mark raw-byte data `binary` in .gitattributes when a `text=auto eol=lf` rule applies. The workflow's own PR run is the test: it must reach the real work, not only build.
rationale: E9.4 (#92): the weekly fuzz workflow passed `fuzz/corpus/parse`, which .gitignore excludes; on the runner libFuzzer exited with 'No such file or directory' before fuzzing, so the criterion 'the E2.2 corpus runs in CI weekly' was not delivered.
